title: Austin's 1908 Public Health & Infrastructure Decisions
summary:
• **Stagnant Water Ordinance Passed**: City Council unanimously approved new regulations prohibiting foul or stagnant water on Austin properties, with penalties for violations—a public health measure addressing sanitation concerns.

• **Circus Damage Deposit Required**: New ordinance proposed requiring circuses and traveling shows to post money deposits to cover damage to city streets, bridges, and property from heavy wagons.

• **Cemetery Space for Confederate Women's Home**: Council granted the Ladies Confederate Home's request for burial space in the City Cemetery.

• **1908 Tax Levy Approved**: Council unanimously passed the annual tax ordinance for the year.

• **Street Car Ordinance Tabled**: A proposal to repeal regulations for street car conductor duties at railroad crossings was postponed, with aldermen split on the decision.

Stagnant Water
The Mayor laid before the Council the substitute ordinance offered by the Ordinance

and providing a penalty for the violation thereof. The ordinance was read the second time,
and passed under suspension of the rule by the following vote: Yeas Aldermen Armstrong,
Crocker, Cumeo, Haynes, Meredith, Miller, Moreland, Petri, Redd, Scott, Smith, Suter &
Wilhelm 13 Nays none.

Tax Levy for 1908
The Mayor laid before the Council an ordinance levying taxes for the year 1908, which was
read the first time and passed under suspension of the rules by the following vote: Yeas
Aldermen Armstrong, Crocker, Cumeo, Haynes, Meredith, Miller, Morel and, Petri, Redd,
Scott, Smith, Suter & Wilhelm 13 Nays none.

Circus Ordinance
By Alderman Wilhelm an ordinance providing for a deposit of money for the purpose
repairing damages done to streets, bridges, culverts and property of the City of Austin by
circuses and traveling shows using wagons heavier than those used in the ordinary
transaction of business within the City of Austin.
The ordinance was read the first time and on motion was referred to the Ordinance
Committee and City Attorney, with instructions to report at the next meeting of the
Council.
